issue.title: chore(toolchain): upgrade Flutter 3.41.9 → 3.44.0 (Dart 3.11.5 → 3.12.0) + dependency triage plan
issue.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **⚠️ VERDICT REVISED (2026-05-31) — read the [deep-research correction comment](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/issues/4846#issuecomment-4585804768) first.**
> A follow-up exhaustive audit (deterministic full-lockfile SDK scan + ~80-agent deep web research, adversarially verified) **overturns the "🟢 GREEN / zero source changes" conclusion below.** The bump is feasible but **not zero-touch**: there is a **hard compile blocker** — the `media_kit_video` git fork won't build on 3.44/Dart 3.12 ([media-kit#1418](https://github.com/media-kit/media-kit/issues/1418)) and must be patched first — plus a `ListTile` debug-assert risk and several deprecation hits. The version-**resolvability** analysis in this body still holds (all 353 lock entries resolve); the "no source changes" claim does **not**. Treat the sections below as the resolvability baseline, and the correction comment as the current verdict.

---

## Summary

This issue proposes upgrading our toolchain from **Flutter 3.41.9 / Dart 3.11.5** → **Flutter 3.44.0 / Dart 3.12.0** (latest stable, released 2026-05-18), and lays out a triaged plan for the dependency tree behind it.

The two efforts are **independent and should be decoupled**: the Flutter bump is low-risk and blocks nothing; dependency updates are optional follow-ups done at our own pace.

@hm21 — flagging you for a sanity check before I start. Two specific questions for you near the bottom (build_runner cap + go_router/riverpod majors). Does this sequencing look right to you, and is there anything in our native/media stack you'd want exercised before we cut over?

---

## Baseline (ground truth, verified against the Flutter release index)

| | Version | Dart | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pinned now | Flutter **3.41.9** | Dart **3.11.5** | 2026-04-30 |
| **Target (latest stable)** | Flutter **3.44.0** | Dart **3.12.0** | 2026-05-18 |
| Latest beta (not proposed) | 3.45.0-0.1.pre | 3.13.0 | 2026-05-21 |

This is **one stable cadence step** (Dart 3.11.5 → 3.12.0, a single minor) — not a major jump.

**Local drift to fix while we're here:** bare `flutter` on at least one dev machine resolves to **3.41.1**, while `mobile/mise.toml` pins **3.41.9**. The upgrade is a good moment to realign mise as the single local authority.

---

## Readiness verdict: 🟢 GREEN — low risk

Audit (4 parallel codebase sweeps + direct pub.dev SDK-constraint checks):

1. **Deprecated/removed APIs — ZERO.** Scanned 2,675 Dart files (lib, all packages, test, integration_test, excluding generated). No `WillPopScope`, `RawKeyboard*`, `textScaleFactor`, `.withOpacity`, `MaterialState*`, or integer `Color` getters. Already on `PopScope` / `withValues(alpha:)` / `TextScaler`. **No source changes required for the bump.**
2. **The `build_runner` "blocker" is a false alarm — verified.** Cap is `>=2.7.1 <2.11.0` (TODO #3142, riverpod_generator `InvalidTypeException`), resolved to 2.10.5. Worry was "does Dart 3.12 force build_runner ≥ 2.11?" Answer from pub.dev: **no.** build_runner 2.10.5 declares `sdk: ^3.7.0` (accepts 3.12); analyzer 8.4.0 is `^3.9.0` (accepts 3.12). **The cap stays as-is — no upstream coordination needed.**
3. **Native toolchain — all above Flutter 3.44 minimums:** iOS deploy 16.0, macOS 13.0, Xcode 26.5, Android AGP 8.9.1 / Kotlin 2.1.0 / Gradle 8.12 / NDK 28.2.13676358 / compileSdk 36 / minSdk 28 / Java 17. (Advisory only: Gradle 8.12 is slightly ahead of 3.44's tested band — already works on 3.41, leave it.)
4. **Two git-pinned deps to compile-check** (no SDK-constraint enforcement): `c2pa_flutter @ 0.0.3` and the `media_kit_video` fork commit. Compile under 3.11 today; Dart 3.12 has no language breaking changes, so low risk — the build/test step proves it.

---

## Complete file inventory for the Flutter bump

Verified by a repo-wide scan — **no hidden second source of truth.**

| File | Lines | Change | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mobile/mise.toml` | 2 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` | **Local toolchain authority** |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_ci.yaml` | 25, 80, 98, 116 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` (×4 jobs) | CI |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_pr_preview_build.yml` | 37 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` | CI |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_service_integration_tests.yaml` | 22 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` | CI |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_web_production_deploy.yml` | 34 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` | CI |
| `.github/workflows/models_ci.yaml` | 27 | `flutter_version: "3.41.9"` → `"3.44.0"` | CI (reusable input) |
| `.github/workflows/sounds_repository.yaml` | 27 | `flutter_version: "3.41.9"` → `"3.44.0"` | CI (reusable input) |
| `codemagic.yaml` | 371, 431, 477, 530, 561, 598 | `flutter: 3.41.9` → `3.44.0` (×6) | App-store builds |
| `mobile/pubspec.yaml` | 22–23 | floor bump (see note) | constraint |
| ~24 `mobile/packages/*/pubspec.yaml` | — | floor bump (see note) | constraint |
| `mobile/.metadata` | 9 | `channel: "beta"` → `"stable"` | drift cleanup (optional) |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | 145–146 | doc text | docs |
| `mobile/pubspec.lock` | — | **regenerated, not hand-edited** | the real artifact |

**Note on the pubspec floors:** `sdk: ^3.11.0` / `flutter: ^3.41.1` are *floors*, not pins — caret ranges already permit 3.44/Dart 3.12, so resolution works without touching them. Raising to `sdk: ^3.12.0` / `flutter: ^3.44.0` is correct hygiene (a contributor on an old SDK gets a clear error instead of a confusing build failure). If we bump the app floor, bump the package floors for consistency.

---

## The 1.0-confidence procedure (order matters)

Change the toolchain authority first, let tooling regenerate the lockfile, prove it builds/tests, **then** fan the pin out to CI.

```bash
# 0. Branch off origin/main
git fetch origin && git checkout -b chore/flutter-3.44 origin/main

# 1. Bump LOCAL authority first, install, realign drift
#    edit mobile/mise.toml: flutter = "3.44.0"
cd mobile && mise install
mise exec -- flutter --version            # confirm 3.44.0 / Dart 3.12.0

# 2. Regenerate the lockfile under the new SDK (the real change)
mise exec -- flutter pub get
git diff pubspec.lock                      # review (expect minimal)

# 3. Regenerate code (build_runner cap stays — verified compatible)
mise exec -- dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs

# 4. Prove it — the gates that turn "should work" into 1.0
mise exec -- flutter analyze lib test integration_test
mise exec -- flutter test
mise exec -- flutter build apk --debug
mise exec -- flutter build ios --no-codesign
mise exec -- flutter build macos
mise exec -- flutter build web

# 5. Only AFTER local is green: bump the pins everywhere (table above)

# 6. Commit lockfile + generated files + version pins together; push; let CI confirm
```

**Confidence scope:** ~1.0 on the *inventory* (exhaustive, verified) and *static compatibility* (deps, APIs, native toolchain, build_runner cap). The one thing no static analysis can give 1.0 on is "compiles + all tests pass" — that's steps 2–4, which is the final piece of the procedure, not optional.

**Product heads-up for the next cycle (not blocking now):** Flutter 3.44 flags **iOS UIScene lifecycle** and **AGP 9 / KGP** as *future* requirements. Neither breaks us today (AGP 8.9.1 + backward-compat), but worth planning.

---

## Dependency tree (separate, decoupled effort)

Queried pub.dev directly for all ~96 hosted direct deps across the workspace.

**Single most important finding:** **every package's latest version still accepts Dart 3.12 / Flutter 3.44 — zero exceptions.** Nothing in the dependency tree blocks the Flutter upgrade. A plain `flutter pub get` after the bump will **not** pull any of the below — they're held by our `^` constraints, so the upgrade PR stays clean. We opt into these explicitly.

Of 96 hosted direct deps: **42 current, 15 patch-behind, 27 minor-behind, 10 major-behind.**

### 🟢 Tier 1 — safe sweep (patches + low-risk minors), one PR
Pure bugfixes, no API changes:
`dio→5.9.2, freezed→3.2.5, image_picker→1.2.2, permission_handler→12.0.2, shared_preferences→2.5.5, uuid→4.5.3, mocktail→1.0.5, equatable→2.0.8, http→1.6.0, json_serializable→6.14.0, json_annotation→4.12.0, flutter_svg→2.3.0, cupertino_icons→1.0.9, async→2.13.1, webview_flutter→4.13.1, flutter_native_splash→2.4.8, skeletonizer→2.1.3, postgres→3.5.11, connectivity_plus→7.1.1, file_selector→1.1.0` + the **5 Firebase** minors (`firebase_core→4.9.0`, `firebase_analytics→12.4.1`, `firebase_crashlytics→5.2.2`, `firebase_messaging→16.2.2`, `firebase_performance→0.11.4+1` — bump as a co-versioned set). `build_runner→2.15.0` only after confirming #3142's riverpod_generator bug is gone (test codegen).

### 🟡 Tier 2 — major bumps, plugin-only (read changelog, likely mechanical)
Breaking changes usually in native setup, not Dart API. Each its own PR:
`device_info_plus 10→13` (+3 majors, biggest gap), `file_picker 10→11`, `flutter_secure_storage 9→10`, `package_info_plus 9→10`, `share_plus 12→13`, `flutter_web_auth_2 4→5`.

### 🔴 Tier 3 — major bumps needing real code review
- **`go_router 16→17`** — routing is load-bearing (typed routes, redirects, ShellRoute). v17 has API changes; needs careful migration + full nav testing.
- **`riverpod_generator + riverpod_annotation 3→4`** — codegen contract change; regenerate everything + verify; couple with runtime `flutter_riverpod 3.0.3→3.3.1`. This is also where the build_runner #3142 cap lives — untangle first.
- **`google_fonts 6→8`** (+2 majors) — API/asset-loading changes; verify Pacifico / Inter / BricolageGrotesque still resolve.

### 📝 Worth a look
`hive_ce 2.6→2.19` (+13 minors — large drift on our persistence layer; changelog scan), `drift 2.31→2.33` (paired with drift_dev, regen), `patrol 4.2→4.6` (+4, integration-test harness), `sqlite3_flutter_libs→0.6.0+eol` (the `+eol` tag is a flag — check what's deprecated).

---

## Proposed sequencing

1. **Ship the Flutter 3.44 bump alone first** — clean, low-risk, unblocks nothing else.
2. **Then Tier 1** as one "dependency housekeeping" PR — fast, high-confidence.
3. **Then Tier 2/3 individually**, each with its own changelog read + targeted tests. Never batch a major bump with anything else (one-line `git bisect` when something breaks).

---

## Questions for @hm21

1. **build_runner cap (#3142):** I verified the cap doesn't block Dart 3.12, so I'd keep it as-is for the bump. But do you want to bundle an attempt to *lift* it (test whether riverpod_generator 4.x fixes the `InvalidTypeException`) into the riverpod 3→4 PR, or keep that entirely separate?
2. **go_router 16→17 + riverpod 3→4:** these are the two Tier-3 items that touch app/generated code. Any preference on order, or known landmines in our routing/state layers I should plan around?
3. **media stack:** anything in `media_kit` / `media_kit_video` fork / `pro_video_editor` / `pro_image_editor` you'd want explicitly exercised on 3.44 before we cut over (beyond the standard build + test)?
4. **Sequencing:** does "Flutter bump solo → Tier 1 sweep → Tier 2/3 individually" match how you'd want this staged?

> Note: confidence is ~1.0 on the inventory and static compatibility; "compiles + tests pass" and the Tier 2/3 "upgrades without breaking our code" claims are exactly what the per-PR build/test gates establish — not assertable statically.

comment.body: @hm21 quick one before I go further: do you want **me** to run `flutter pub upgrade --major-versions` and prep the dependency-bump diff (you'd then device-test file_picker etc. + build the platforms), or would you rather drive the whole deps-bump + on-device pass yourself since you already have 3.44.0 running locally? Whichever's faster for you — just don't want us both touching the deps at once. (Also: confirm the media_kit_video SHA to ship — keep `6b71849` or a newer fork commit?)

issue.body: Closes #4850 ## Description Discussed on discord [here](https://discord.com/channels/1470168817589158040/1470255950408454164/1510133586047537223) Adds a **hold-to-record** mode to the video recorder, allowing users to start recording by pressing and holding the shutter button and stop by releasing it — in addition to the existing tap-to-record behaviour. **Related Issue:** ### Changes - **`VideoRecorderBloc`** — new `holdToRecord` flag in state; updated start/stop logic to handle press-down / release events - **`VideoRecorderState`** — added `holdToRecord` field - **`HoldToRecordPreferenceService`** — new service backed by `SharedPreferences` to persist the user's preference - **`preferencesProviders`** — exposes the new service via Riverpod - **`GeneralSettingsScreen`** — toggle to enable / disable hold-to-record - **`VideoRecorderClassicStack`** / **`ShutterGestureDetector`** / **`VideoRecorderRecordButton`** — wired up press/release gesture handling - **Localizations** — new `cameraSettingsHoldToRecord` key added to all 20 supported locales and generated files regenerated ## Out of Scope None — follow-up could include hold-to-record support for the web recorder if needed. ## Verification - `flutter analyze` — clean - `flutter test mobile/test/blocs/video_recorder/` — green - `flutter test mobile/test/screens/settings/` — green - `flutter test mobile/test/services/hold_to_record_preference_service_test.dart` — green - `flutter test mobile/test/widgets/video_recorder/` — green - Manually tested tap-to-record and hold-to-record modes on iOS Simulator and Android Emulator ## Type of Change - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

issue.title: chore(toolchain): upgrade Flutter 3.41.9 → 3.44.0 (Dart 3.11.5 → 3.12.0) + dependency triage plan
issue.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **⚠️ VERDICT REVISED (2026-05-31) — read the [deep-research correction comment](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/issues/4846#issuecomment-4585804768) first.**
> A follow-up exhaustive audit (deterministic full-lockfile SDK scan + ~80-agent deep web research, adversarially verified) **overturns the "🟢 GREEN / zero source changes" conclusion below.** The bump is feasible but **not zero-touch**: there is a **hard compile blocker** — the `media_kit_video` git fork won't build on 3.44/Dart 3.12 ([media-kit#1418](https://github.com/media-kit/media-kit/issues/1418)) and must be patched first — plus a `ListTile` debug-assert risk and several deprecation hits. The version-**resolvability** analysis in this body still holds (all 353 lock entries resolve); the "no source changes" claim does **not**. Treat the sections below as the resolvability baseline, and the correction comment as the current verdict.

---

## Summary

This issue proposes upgrading our toolchain from **Flutter 3.41.9 / Dart 3.11.5** → **Flutter 3.44.0 / Dart 3.12.0** (latest stable, released 2026-05-18), and lays out a triaged plan for the dependency tree behind it.

The two efforts are **independent and should be decoupled**: the Flutter bump is low-risk and blocks nothing; dependency updates are optional follow-ups done at our own pace.

@hm21 — flagging you for a sanity check before I start. Two specific questions for you near the bottom (build_runner cap + go_router/riverpod majors). Does this sequencing look right to you, and is there anything in our native/media stack you'd want exercised before we cut over?

---

## Baseline (ground truth, verified against the Flutter release index)

| | Version | Dart | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pinned now | Flutter **3.41.9** | Dart **3.11.5** | 2026-04-30 |
| **Target (latest stable)** | Flutter **3.44.0** | Dart **3.12.0** | 2026-05-18 |
| Latest beta (not proposed) | 3.45.0-0.1.pre | 3.13.0 | 2026-05-21 |

This is **one stable cadence step** (Dart 3.11.5 → 3.12.0, a single minor) — not a major jump.

**Local drift to fix while we're here:** bare `flutter` on at least one dev machine resolves to **3.41.1**, while `mobile/mise.toml` pins **3.41.9**. The upgrade is a good moment to realign mise as the single local authority.

---

## Readiness verdict: 🟢 GREEN — low risk

Audit (4 parallel codebase sweeps + direct pub.dev SDK-constraint checks):

1. **Deprecated/removed APIs — ZERO.** Scanned 2,675 Dart files (lib, all packages, test, integration_test, excluding generated). No `WillPopScope`, `RawKeyboard*`, `textScaleFactor`, `.withOpacity`, `MaterialState*`, or integer `Color` getters. Already on `PopScope` / `withValues(alpha:)` / `TextScaler`. **No source changes required for the bump.**
2. **The `build_runner` "blocker" is a false alarm — verified.** Cap is `>=2.7.1 <2.11.0` (TODO #3142, riverpod_generator `InvalidTypeException`), resolved to 2.10.5. Worry was "does Dart 3.12 force build_runner ≥ 2.11?" Answer from pub.dev: **no.** build_runner 2.10.5 declares `sdk: ^3.7.0` (accepts 3.12); analyzer 8.4.0 is `^3.9.0` (accepts 3.12). **The cap stays as-is — no upstream coordination needed.**
3. **Native toolchain — all above Flutter 3.44 minimums:** iOS deploy 16.0, macOS 13.0, Xcode 26.5, Android AGP 8.9.1 / Kotlin 2.1.0 / Gradle 8.12 / NDK 28.2.13676358 / compileSdk 36 / minSdk 28 / Java 17. (Advisory only: Gradle 8.12 is slightly ahead of 3.44's tested band — already works on 3.41, leave it.)
4. **Two git-pinned deps to compile-check** (no SDK-constraint enforcement): `c2pa_flutter @ 0.0.3` and the `media_kit_video` fork commit. Compile under 3.11 today; Dart 3.12 has no language breaking changes, so low risk — the build/test step proves it.

---

## Complete file inventory for the Flutter bump

Verified by a repo-wide scan — **no hidden second source of truth.**

| File | Lines | Change | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mobile/mise.toml` | 2 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` | **Local toolchain authority** |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_ci.yaml` | 25, 80, 98, 116 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` (×4 jobs) | CI |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_pr_preview_build.yml` | 37 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` | CI |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_service_integration_tests.yaml` | 22 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` | CI |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_web_production_deploy.yml` | 34 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` | CI |
| `.github/workflows/models_ci.yaml` | 27 | `flutter_version: "3.41.9"` → `"3.44.0"` | CI (reusable input) |
| `.github/workflows/sounds_repository.yaml` | 27 | `flutter_version: "3.41.9"` → `"3.44.0"` | CI (reusable input) |
| `codemagic.yaml` | 371, 431, 477, 530, 561, 598 | `flutter: 3.41.9` → `3.44.0` (×6) | App-store builds |
| `mobile/pubspec.yaml` | 22–23 | floor bump (see note) | constraint |
| ~24 `mobile/packages/*/pubspec.yaml` | — | floor bump (see note) | constraint |
| `mobile/.metadata` | 9 | `channel: "beta"` → `"stable"` | drift cleanup (optional) |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | 145–146 | doc text | docs |
| `mobile/pubspec.lock` | — | **regenerated, not hand-edited** | the real artifact |

**Note on the pubspec floors:** `sdk: ^3.11.0` / `flutter: ^3.41.1` are *floors*, not pins — caret ranges already permit 3.44/Dart 3.12, so resolution works without touching them. Raising to `sdk: ^3.12.0` / `flutter: ^3.44.0` is correct hygiene (a contributor on an old SDK gets a clear error instead of a confusing build failure). If we bump the app floor, bump the package floors for consistency.

---

## The 1.0-confidence procedure (order matters)

Change the toolchain authority first, let tooling regenerate the lockfile, prove it builds/tests, **then** fan the pin out to CI.

```bash
# 0. Branch off origin/main
git fetch origin && git checkout -b chore/flutter-3.44 origin/main

# 1. Bump LOCAL authority first, install, realign drift
#    edit mobile/mise.toml: flutter = "3.44.0"
cd mobile && mise install
mise exec -- flutter --version            # confirm 3.44.0 / Dart 3.12.0

# 2. Regenerate the lockfile under the new SDK (the real change)
mise exec -- flutter pub get
git diff pubspec.lock                      # review (expect minimal)

# 3. Regenerate code (build_runner cap stays — verified compatible)
mise exec -- dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs

# 4. Prove it — the gates that turn "should work" into 1.0
mise exec -- flutter analyze lib test integration_test
mise exec -- flutter test
mise exec -- flutter build apk --debug
mise exec -- flutter build ios --no-codesign
mise exec -- flutter build macos
mise exec -- flutter build web

# 5. Only AFTER local is green: bump the pins everywhere (table above)

# 6. Commit lockfile + generated files + version pins together; push; let CI confirm
```

**Confidence scope:** ~1.0 on the *inventory* (exhaustive, verified) and *static compatibility* (deps, APIs, native toolchain, build_runner cap). The one thing no static analysis can give 1.0 on is "compiles + all tests pass" — that's steps 2–4, which is the final piece of the procedure, not optional.

**Product heads-up for the next cycle (not blocking now):** Flutter 3.44 flags **iOS UIScene lifecycle** and **AGP 9 / KGP** as *future* requirements. Neither breaks us today (AGP 8.9.1 + backward-compat), but worth planning.

---

## Dependency tree (separate, decoupled effort)

Queried pub.dev directly for all ~96 hosted direct deps across the workspace.

**Single most important finding:** **every package's latest version still accepts Dart 3.12 / Flutter 3.44 — zero exceptions.** Nothing in the dependency tree blocks the Flutter upgrade. A plain `flutter pub get` after the bump will **not** pull any of the below — they're held by our `^` constraints, so the upgrade PR stays clean. We opt into these explicitly.

Of 96 hosted direct deps: **42 current, 15 patch-behind, 27 minor-behind, 10 major-behind.**

### 🟢 Tier 1 — safe sweep (patches + low-risk minors), one PR
Pure bugfixes, no API changes:
`dio→5.9.2, freezed→3.2.5, image_picker→1.2.2, permission_handler→12.0.2, shared_preferences→2.5.5, uuid→4.5.3, mocktail→1.0.5, equatable→2.0.8, http→1.6.0, json_serializable→6.14.0, json_annotation→4.12.0, flutter_svg→2.3.0, cupertino_icons→1.0.9, async→2.13.1, webview_flutter→4.13.1, flutter_native_splash→2.4.8, skeletonizer→2.1.3, postgres→3.5.11, connectivity_plus→7.1.1, file_selector→1.1.0` + the **5 Firebase** minors (`firebase_core→4.9.0`, `firebase_analytics→12.4.1`, `firebase_crashlytics→5.2.2`, `firebase_messaging→16.2.2`, `firebase_performance→0.11.4+1` — bump as a co-versioned set). `build_runner→2.15.0` only after confirming #3142's riverpod_generator bug is gone (test codegen).

### 🟡 Tier 2 — major bumps, plugin-only (read changelog, likely mechanical)
Breaking changes usually in native setup, not Dart API. Each its own PR:
`device_info_plus 10→13` (+3 majors, biggest gap), `file_picker 10→11`, `flutter_secure_storage 9→10`, `package_info_plus 9→10`, `share_plus 12→13`, `flutter_web_auth_2 4→5`.

### 🔴 Tier 3 — major bumps needing real code review
- **`go_router 16→17`** — routing is load-bearing (typed routes, redirects, ShellRoute). v17 has API changes; needs careful migration + full nav testing.
- **`riverpod_generator + riverpod_annotation 3→4`** — codegen contract change; regenerate everything + verify; couple with runtime `flutter_riverpod 3.0.3→3.3.1`. This is also where the build_runner #3142 cap lives — untangle first.
- **`google_fonts 6→8`** (+2 majors) — API/asset-loading changes; verify Pacifico / Inter / BricolageGrotesque still resolve.

### 📝 Worth a look
`hive_ce 2.6→2.19` (+13 minors — large drift on our persistence layer; changelog scan), `drift 2.31→2.33` (paired with drift_dev, regen), `patrol 4.2→4.6` (+4, integration-test harness), `sqlite3_flutter_libs→0.6.0+eol` (the `+eol` tag is a flag — check what's deprecated).

---

## Proposed sequencing

1. **Ship the Flutter 3.44 bump alone first** — clean, low-risk, unblocks nothing else.
2. **Then Tier 1** as one "dependency housekeeping" PR — fast, high-confidence.
3. **Then Tier 2/3 individually**, each with its own changelog read + targeted tests. Never batch a major bump with anything else (one-line `git bisect` when something breaks).

---

## Questions for @hm21

1. **build_runner cap (#3142):** I verified the cap doesn't block Dart 3.12, so I'd keep it as-is for the bump. But do you want to bundle an attempt to *lift* it (test whether riverpod_generator 4.x fixes the `InvalidTypeException`) into the riverpod 3→4 PR, or keep that entirely separate?
2. **go_router 16→17 + riverpod 3→4:** these are the two Tier-3 items that touch app/generated code. Any preference on order, or known landmines in our routing/state layers I should plan around?
3. **media stack:** anything in `media_kit` / `media_kit_video` fork / `pro_video_editor` / `pro_image_editor` you'd want explicitly exercised on 3.44 before we cut over (beyond the standard build + test)?
4. **Sequencing:** does "Flutter bump solo → Tier 1 sweep → Tier 2/3 individually" match how you'd want this staged?

> Note: confidence is ~1.0 on the inventory and static compatibility; "compiles + tests pass" and the Tier 2/3 "upgrades without breaking our code" claims are exactly what the per-PR build/test gates establish — not assertable statically.

comment.body:
@realmeylisdev actually I already updated Flutter to version 3.44.0 and everything works perfectly fine so far on my machine ;)

What we still need to do, so we can also build the app on Android and not only run it in debug mode, is update the Gradle version to at least 8.14.0 and the Kotlin version to at least 2.2.20.

MediaKit also doesn’t seem to cause any issues. Just note that we forked MediaKit ourselves, so you should find the repository here in the organization: https://github.com/divinevideo/media-kit

I’d recommend upgrading everything at once. That means first updating all Flutter versions in the CI and then updating all dependencies in the pubspec.yaml to the highest possible versions. This should only take a couple of minutes.

After that, it’s very important to properly test everything you updated on a real device. For example, check if file-picker still works correctly. Once that is done, you can try building for every platform except Windows. If all of that works as well, it should be ready for a PR. 

In the worst case, we may need to pin down some packages, but in my experience that rarely happens. Also, changelogs are not always perfectly maintained, so the best approach is always to test everything on a real device to make sure it still works properly.

issue.title: feat: add timeline markers for video and audio sync

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
### What would you like?

Add the ability to place markers along the video and audio timeline during editing. Markers could be used to flag important moments like sound effects, impacts, transitions, or cuts so users can quickly align clips and audio without repeatedly scrubbing through the timeline.

### How would this be useful for you?

This would make syncing audio effects much faster and more accurate, especially when fixing missing or desynced audio. Instead of constantly rewinding and retrying adjustments, users could mark key moments and line everything up visually.

### When would you use this?

When editing clips with timed sound effects like Vine Booms, smashes, transitions, or music beats where precise sync matters.

### Anything else?

It could be helpful if markers supported labels or different colors for audio vs video events.

This was requested on discord [here](https://discord.com/channels/1470168817589158040/1470256031434149953/1510445689153388654)

## The 1.0-confidence procedure (order matters)

Change the toolchain authority first, let tooling regenerate the lockfile, prove it builds/tests, **then** fan the pin out to CI.

```bash
# 0. Branch off origin/main
git fetch origin && git checkout -b chore/flutter-3.44 origin/main

# 1. Bump LOCAL authority first, install, realign drift
#    edit mobile/mise.toml: flutter = "3.44.0"
cd mobile && mise install
mise exec -- flutter --version            # confirm 3.44.0 / Dart 3.12.0

# 2. Regenerate the lockfile under the new SDK (the real change)
mise exec -- flutter pub get
git diff pubspec.lock                      # review (expect minimal)

# 3. Regenerate code (build_runner cap stays — verified compatible)
mise exec -- dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs

# 4. Prove it — the gates that turn "should work" into 1.0
mise exec -- flutter analyze lib test integration_test
mise exec -- flutter test
mise exec -- flutter build apk --debug
mise exec -- flutter build ios --no-codesign
mise exec -- flutter build macos
mise exec -- flutter build web

# 5. Only AFTER local is green: bump the pins everywhere (table above)

# 6. Commit lockfile + generated files + version pins together; push; let CI confirm
```

**Confidence scope:** ~1.0 on the *inventory* (exhaustive, verified) and *static compatibility* (deps, APIs, native toolchain, build_runner cap). The one thing no static analysis can give 1.0 on is "compiles + all tests pass" — that's steps 2–4, which is the final piece of the procedure, not optional.

**Product heads-up for the next cycle (not blocking now):** Flutter 3.44 flags **iOS UIScene lifecycle** and **AGP 9 / KGP** as *future* requirements. Neither breaks us today (AGP 8.9.1 + backward-compat), but worth planning.

---

## Dependency tree (separate, decoupled effort)

Queried pub.dev directly for all ~96 hosted direct deps across the workspace.

**Single most important finding:** **every package's latest version still accepts Dart 3.12 / Flutter 3.44 — zero exceptions.** Nothing in the dependency tree blocks the Flutter upgrade. A plain `flutter pub get` after the bump will **not** pull any of the below — they're held by our `^` constraints, so the upgrade PR stays clean. We opt into these explicitly.

Of 96 hosted direct deps: **42 current, 15 patch-behind, 27 minor-behind, 10 major-behind.**

### 🟢 Tier 1 — safe sweep (patches + low-risk minors), one PR
Pure bugfixes, no API changes:
`dio→5.9.2, freezed→3.2.5, image_picker→1.2.2, permission_handler→12.0.2, shared_preferences→2.5.5, uuid→4.5.3, mocktail→1.0.5, equatable→2.0.8, http→1.6.0, json_serializable→6.14.0, json_annotation→4.12.0, flutter_svg→2.3.0, cupertino_icons→1.0.9, async→2.13.1, webview_flutter→4.13.1, flutter_native_splash→2.4.8, skeletonizer→2.1.3, postgres→3.5.11, connectivity_plus→7.1.1, file_selector→1.1.0` + the **5 Firebase** minors (`firebase_core→4.9.0`, `firebase_analytics→12.4.1`, `firebase_crashlytics→5.2.2`, `firebase_messaging→16.2.2`, `firebase_performance→0.11.4+1` — bump as a co-versioned set). `build_runner→2.15.0` only after confirming #3142's riverpod_generator bug is gone (test codegen).

### 🟡 Tier 2 — major bumps, plugin-only (read changelog, likely mechanical)
Breaking changes usually in native setup, not Dart API. Each its own PR:
`device_info_plus 10→13` (+3 majors, biggest gap), `file_picker 10→11`, `flutter_secure_storage 9→10`, `package_info_plus 9→10`, `share_plus 12→13`, `flutter_web_auth_2 4→5`.

### 🔴 Tier 3 — major bumps needing real code review
- **`go_router 16→17`** — routing is load-bearing (typed routes, redirects, ShellRoute). v17 has API changes; needs careful migration + full nav testing.
- **`riverpod_generator + riverpod_annotation 3→4`** — codegen contract change; regenerate everything + verify; couple with runtime `flutter_riverpod 3.0.3→3.3.1`. This is also where the build_runner #3142 cap lives — untangle first.
- **`google_fonts 6→8`** (+2 majors) — API/asset-loading changes; verify Pacifico / Inter / BricolageGrotesque still resolve.

### 📝 Worth a look
`hive_ce 2.6→2.19` (+13 minors — large drift on our persistence layer; changelog scan), `drift 2.31→2.33` (paired with drift_dev, regen), `patrol 4.2→4.6` (+4, integration-test harness), `sqlite3_flutter_libs→0.6.0+eol` (the `+eol` tag is a flag — check what's deprecated).

---

## Proposed sequencing

1. **Ship the Flutter 3.44 bump alone first** — clean, low-risk, unblocks nothing else.
2. **Then Tier 1** as one "dependency housekeeping" PR — fast, high-confidence.
3. **Then Tier 2/3 individually**, each with its own changelog read + targeted tests. Never batch a major bump with anything else (one-line `git bisect` when something breaks).

---

## Questions for @hm21

1. **build_runner cap (#3142):** I verified the cap doesn't block Dart 3.12, so I'd keep it as-is for the bump. But do you want to bundle an attempt to *lift* it (test whether riverpod_generator 4.x fixes the `InvalidTypeException`) into the riverpod 3→4 PR, or keep that entirely separate?
2. **go_router 16→17 + riverpod 3→4:** these are the two Tier-3 items that touch app/generated code. Any preference on order, or known landmines in our routing/state layers I should plan around?
3. **media stack:** anything in `media_kit` / `media_kit_video` fork / `pro_video_editor` / `pro_image_editor` you'd want explicitly exercised on 3.44 before we cut over (beyond the standard build + test)?
4. **Sequencing:** does "Flutter bump solo → Tier 1 sweep → Tier 2/3 individually" match how you'd want this staged?

> Note: confidence is ~1.0 on the inventory and static compatibility; "compiles + tests pass" and the Tier 2/3 "upgrades without breaking our code" claims are exactly what the per-PR build/test gates establish — not assertable statically.

## ⚠️ Deep-research update — correcting the verdict above

@hm21 — I ran an exhaustive follow-up (deterministic full-lockfile SDK scan + ~80-agent deep web research across every dependency, the Flutter/Dart release notes, and a codebase re-scan, with adversarial verification). **It overturns the "🟢 GREEN / zero source changes" claim in the original issue body. Please read this before the earlier section.**

Honest headline: the bump is **feasible but NOT zero-touch**. There is **one hard compile blocker** that fails `flutter build` outright, plus a handful of deprecation/behavior hits to triage. Confidence the "zero-change" claim is wrong: **0.9** (adversarially verified).

---

### Premise correction first
There is **no Flutter 3.42 or 3.43 stable** — the official release index jumps **3.41 → 3.44** (`release-notes-3.42.0` 404s). So this is a single-step **3.41.9 → 3.44.0** (Dart 3.11.5 → 3.12.0) bump, and **both** the 3.41 *and* 3.44 breaking-change sections apply cumulatively.

### Deterministic layer (proven, ~1.0)
Parsed the **entire 353-entry `pubspec.lock`** (341 hosted + 2 git + 2 path + 8 SDK) and checked each resolved version's SDK constraint against pub.dev: **every hosted + transitive package resolves under Dart 3.12.0 AND Flutter 3.44.0 — zero exceptions.** (The ~23 packages declaring `<3.0.0` are the standard Dart-3 null-safety compat case — they already build today on 3.11.5.) So **version resolution is not the risk.** The risk is everything resolution *can't* see.

---

## 🔴 BLOCKER — `media_kit_video` fork will not compile

This is the one that fails the build. Confirmed in the codebase: `mobile/pubspec.yaml:310` pins
```yaml
media_kit_video:
  git: { url: https://github.com/divinevideo/media-kit, ref: 6b718491261e40ddebf1fe9b880b3d5d30205ee0, path: media_kit_video }
```
(the texture-rotation fix for media-kit#627).

Upstream **[media-kit#1418](https://github.com/media-kit/media-kit/issues/1418)** ("iOS build errors after upgrading to Flutter 3.44.0", OPEN, 3 users) reports `lib/src/video/video_texture.dart` failing to compile under Flutter 3.44/Dart 3.12 — ambiguous `VideoState` / `VideoControlsBuilder` typing surfaced by Dart 3.12's stricter analysis. The reporter confirms it **reproduces on upstream `main`**, and there is **no fixed pub release** (latest is 2.0.1, same major we fork). Because our fork at `6b71849` inherits that exact file, it is very likely affected.

**Action (gating):** rebase/patch the `divinevideo/media-kit` fork to fix the `video_texture.dart` typing on 3.44/Dart 3.12 *before* the toolchain bump can build at all. The deterministic "lock resolves" proof structurally **cannot** cover this — git deps carry no SDK constraint. This needs an actual `flutter build`.

---

## 🟠 Likely CI/test-suite failure — `ListTile` debug assert

Flutter 3.44's [`list-tile-color-warning`](https://docs.flutter.dev/release/breaking-changes) adds a **debug assert** when a `ListTile` sits directly inside a colored ancestor (`ColoredBox` / `Container(color:)` / `Material(color:)`). It **compiles fine but throws in debug runs and widget tests** — so it can redden CI even when release builds work. **26 files** use `ListTile` (verified by grep; the deep-research pass estimated 31) — audit the ones with a colored parent.

## 🟡 Deprecation / behavior hits (compile with warnings; triage)
Reported by the codebase re-scan (verify exact sites during the build):
- **`onReorder` deprecated** (→ onReorderStart/Move/End) — **6 video-editor timeline files**.
- **`cacheExtent` deprecated** — `lib/widgets/library/clips_tab.dart`.
- **`RawMenuAnchor` close-order behavior change** (runtime focus/dismiss) — `message_input_bar.dart` (chat composer); verify behavior.
- **Android built-in-Kotlin / AGP 9 migration** — `android/settings.gradle.kts` manually applies `org.jetbrains.kotlin.android` 2.1.0; Flutter 3.44 flags this (likely a *warning* on our AGP 8.9.1, not a failure — but the android-gradle verification agent stalled, so this is **unconfirmed by an actual build**).
- **Native plugin toolchain-floor mismatches:** `connectivity_plus 7.0.0` and `android_intent_plus 6.0.0` both *state* min AGP 8.12.1 / Gradle 8.13 / Kotlin 2.2.0; repo is AGP 8.9.1 / Gradle 8.12 / Kotlin 2.1.0. These are recommended floors (already resolving today), most likely warnings — confirm with a real `flutter build apk`.
- **`flutter_secure_storage 9.2.4`:** keep the version (a 10.x bump risks failing to decrypt stored secrets/nsec), but it needs release-only **R8/Tink keep-rules** (#839) and a Podfile **IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET** pin for the Xcode 16 dyld startup crash (#794/#901) — both only show in `--release`/on-device.

## 🟢 Cleared
- **`IconData` marked `final`** (3.44): no `extends/implements IconData` anywhere — safe.
- **Dart 3.12:** the only true SDK breaking change is `dart:js_interop`'s `isA` relocation — **web/JS-interop only**, negligible for this mobile app. One new lint (`simple_directive_paths`) will **not** fire because `very_good_analysis` is pinned `^10.2.0` (ruleset frozen). The big null-safety/dead-code analyzer tightening was **Dart 3.9**, already active on 3.11.5 — it will **not** re-fire.

---

## Dependency verdict tally (deep web research)
**1 RED** (media_kit family) · **~26 YELLOW** (works on resolved version, mostly "stay-put"; native floor / release-only watch-items) · **~65 GREEN**. Firebase suite: all build-resolvable on the pinned config; the active 3.44 "GeneratedPluginRegistrant can't find FlutterFire classes" cluster ([flutter#186800](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/186800)) is **AGP-9-only** and we sidestep it on AGP 8.9.1 — but validate with a real Android release build.

## Honest confidence statement
- **~1.0:** the file inventory and version-**resolvability**.
- **NOT 1.0 and not reachable by research:** "compiles + analyzes + tests + builds clean on all platforms." The media_kit fork blocker, the ListTile assert, the deprecation warnings, and the native-toolchain floors are exactly the class of thing only an **actual `flutter pub get` → `build_runner` → `analyze` → `test` → per-platform `build`** run on the 3.44 toolchain can close. Two research agents also stalled (android-gradle inspection; the synthesis pass), so the Android-build and a few leaf deps are "covered indirectly, not independently re-confirmed."

## Revised pre-flight checklist
1. **Fix the `media_kit_video` fork first** (rebase/patch `video_texture.dart` for 3.44/Dart 3.12). Nothing else matters until this builds.
2. Bump toolchain (`mise.toml` → 3.44.0), `flutter pub get`, confirm lock unchanged.
3. `dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` + diff generated files.
4. `dart format .` in a dedicated commit (formatter churn is the usual Format-gate surprise).
5. `flutter analyze` vs the 3.11.5 baseline; triage onReorder/cacheExtent warnings.
6. `flutter test` — watch for the **ListTile debug assert** in widget tests.
7. Per-platform builds: `apk` (R8/Tink rules; AGP/Kotlin floors), `ios --no-codesign` (Podfile deployment-target pin; UIScene warnings), `macos`, `web`. Smoke-test **video playback** (media_kit) and the **chat composer menu**.
8. Bump the CI/codemagic pins (8 sites) + pubspec floors **only after local is green**.

**Questions for you, @hm21:** (1) Can you take the `media_kit_video` fork rebase, or point me at who owns that fork? It's the gating item. (2) Is upstream media-kit#1418 something you'd rather wait on than carry another fork patch? (3) Any objection to staging it as: *fork fix → toolchain bump → deprecation cleanup*, each its own commit?

issue.title: chore(toolchain): upgrade Flutter 3.41.9 → 3.44.0 (Dart 3.11.5 → 3.12.0) + dependency triage plan
issue.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **⚠️ VERDICT REVISED (2026-05-31) — read the [deep-research correction comment](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/issues/4846#issuecomment-4585804768) first.**
> A follow-up exhaustive audit (deterministic full-lockfile SDK scan + ~80-agent deep web research, adversarially verified) **overturns the "🟢 GREEN / zero source changes" conclusion below.** The bump is feasible but **not zero-touch**: there is a **hard compile blocker** — the `media_kit_video` git fork won't build on 3.44/Dart 3.12 ([media-kit#1418](https://github.com/media-kit/media-kit/issues/1418)) and must be patched first — plus a `ListTile` debug-assert risk and several deprecation hits. The version-**resolvability** analysis in this body still holds (all 353 lock entries resolve); the "no source changes" claim does **not**. Treat the sections below as the resolvability baseline, and the correction comment as the current verdict.

---

## Summary

This issue proposes upgrading our toolchain from **Flutter 3.41.9 / Dart 3.11.5** → **Flutter 3.44.0 / Dart 3.12.0** (latest stable, released 2026-05-18), and lays out a triaged plan for the dependency tree behind it.

The two efforts are **independent and should be decoupled**: the Flutter bump is low-risk and blocks nothing; dependency updates are optional follow-ups done at our own pace.

@hm21 — flagging you for a sanity check before I start. Two specific questions for you near the bottom (build_runner cap + go_router/riverpod majors). Does this sequencing look right to you, and is there anything in our native/media stack you'd want exercised before we cut over?

---

## Baseline (ground truth, verified against the Flutter release index)

| | Version | Dart | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pinned now | Flutter **3.41.9** | Dart **3.11.5** | 2026-04-30 |
| **Target (latest stable)** | Flutter **3.44.0** | Dart **3.12.0** | 2026-05-18 |
| Latest beta (not proposed) | 3.45.0-0.1.pre | 3.13.0 | 2026-05-21 |

This is **one stable cadence step** (Dart 3.11.5 → 3.12.0, a single minor) — not a major jump.

**Local drift to fix while we're here:** bare `flutter` on at least one dev machine resolves to **3.41.1**, while `mobile/mise.toml` pins **3.41.9**. The upgrade is a good moment to realign mise as the single local authority.

---

## Readiness verdict: 🟢 GREEN — low risk

Audit (4 parallel codebase sweeps + direct pub.dev SDK-constraint checks):

1. **Deprecated/removed APIs — ZERO.** Scanned 2,675 Dart files (lib, all packages, test, integration_test, excluding generated). No `WillPopScope`, `RawKeyboard*`, `textScaleFactor`, `.withOpacity`, `MaterialState*`, or integer `Color` getters. Already on `PopScope` / `withValues(alpha:)` / `TextScaler`. **No source changes required for the bump.**
2. **The `build_runner` "blocker" is a false alarm — verified.** Cap is `>=2.7.1 <2.11.0` (TODO #3142, riverpod_generator `InvalidTypeException`), resolved to 2.10.5. Worry was "does Dart 3.12 force build_runner ≥ 2.11?" Answer from pub.dev: **no.** build_runner 2.10.5 declares `sdk: ^3.7.0` (accepts 3.12); analyzer 8.4.0 is `^3.9.0` (accepts 3.12). **The cap stays as-is — no upstream coordination needed.**
3. **Native toolchain — all above Flutter 3.44 minimums:** iOS deploy 16.0, macOS 13.0, Xcode 26.5, Android AGP 8.9.1 / Kotlin 2.1.0 / Gradle 8.12 / NDK 28.2.13676358 / compileSdk 36 / minSdk 28 / Java 17. (Advisory only: Gradle 8.12 is slightly ahead of 3.44's tested band — already works on 3.41, leave it.)
4. **Two git-pinned deps to compile-check** (no SDK-constraint enforcement): `c2pa_flutter @ 0.0.3` and the `media_kit_video` fork commit. Compile under 3.11 today; Dart 3.12 has no language breaking changes, so low risk — the build/test step proves it.

---

## Complete file inventory for the Flutter bump

Verified by a repo-wide scan — **no hidden second source of truth.**

| File | Lines | Change | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mobile/mise.toml` | 2 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` | **Local toolchain authority** |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_ci.yaml` | 25, 80, 98, 116 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` (×4 jobs) | CI |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_pr_preview_build.yml` | 37 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` | CI |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_service_integration_tests.yaml` | 22 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` | CI |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_web_production_deploy.yml` | 34 | `3.41.9` → `3.44.0` | CI |
| `.github/workflows/models_ci.yaml` | 27 | `flutter_version: "3.41.9"` → `"3.44.0"` | CI (reusable input) |
| `.github/workflows/sounds_repository.yaml` | 27 | `flutter_version: "3.41.9"` → `"3.44.0"` | CI (reusable input) |
| `codemagic.yaml` | 371, 431, 477, 530, 561, 598 | `flutter: 3.41.9` → `3.44.0` (×6) | App-store builds |
| `mobile/pubspec.yaml` | 22–23 | floor bump (see note) | constraint |
| ~24 `mobile/packages/*/pubspec.yaml` | — | floor bump (see note) | constraint |
| `mobile/.metadata` | 9 | `channel: "beta"` → `"stable"` | drift cleanup (optional) |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | 145–146 | doc text | docs |
| `mobile/pubspec.lock` | — | **regenerated, not hand-edited** | the real artifact |

**Note on the pubspec floors:** `sdk: ^3.11.0` / `flutter: ^3.41.1` are *floors*, not pins — caret ranges already permit 3.44/Dart 3.12, so resolution works without touching them. Raising to `sdk: ^3.12.0` / `flutter: ^3.44.0` is correct hygiene (a contributor on an old SDK gets a clear error instead of a confusing build failure). If we bump the app floor, bump the package floors for consistency.

---

## The 1.0-confidence procedure (order matters)

Change the toolchain authority first, let tooling regenerate the lockfile, prove it builds/tests, **then** fan the pin out to CI.

```bash
# 0. Branch off origin/main
git fetch origin && git checkout -b chore/flutter-3.44 origin/main

# 1. Bump LOCAL authority first, install, realign drift
#    edit mobile/mise.toml: flutter = "3.44.0"
cd mobile && mise install
mise exec -- flutter --version            # confirm 3.44.0 / Dart 3.12.0

# 2. Regenerate the lockfile under the new SDK (the real change)
mise exec -- flutter pub get
git diff pubspec.lock                      # review (expect minimal)

# 3. Regenerate code (build_runner cap stays — verified compatible)
mise exec -- dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs

# 4. Prove it — the gates that turn "should work" into 1.0
mise exec -- flutter analyze lib test integration_test
mise exec -- flutter test
mise exec -- flutter build apk --debug
mise exec -- flutter build ios --no-codesign
mise exec -- flutter build macos
mise exec -- flutter build web

# 5. Only AFTER local is green: bump the pins everywhere (table above)

# 6. Commit lockfile + generated files + version pins together; push; let CI confirm
```

**Confidence scope:** ~1.0 on the *inventory* (exhaustive, verified) and *static compatibility* (deps, APIs, native toolchain, build_runner cap). The one thing no static analysis can give 1.0 on is "compiles + all tests pass" — that's steps 2–4, which is the final piece of the procedure, not optional.

**Product heads-up for the next cycle (not blocking now):** Flutter 3.44 flags **iOS UIScene lifecycle** and **AGP 9 / KGP** as *future* requirements. Neither breaks us today (AGP 8.9.1 + backward-compat), but worth planning.

---

## Dependency tree (separate, decoupled effort)

Queried pub.dev directly for all ~96 hosted direct deps across the workspace.

**Single most important finding:** **every package's latest version still accepts Dart 3.12 / Flutter 3.44 — zero exceptions.** Nothing in the dependency tree blocks the Flutter upgrade. A plain `flutter pub get` after the bump will **not** pull any of the below — they're held by our `^` constraints, so the upgrade PR stays clean. We opt into these explicitly.

Of 96 hosted direct deps: **42 current, 15 patch-behind, 27 minor-behind, 10 major-behind.**

### 🟢 Tier 1 — safe sweep (patches + low-risk minors), one PR
Pure bugfixes, no API changes:
`dio→5.9.2, freezed→3.2.5, image_picker→1.2.2, permission_handler→12.0.2, shared_preferences→2.5.5, uuid→4.5.3, mocktail→1.0.5, equatable→2.0.8, http→1.6.0, json_serializable→6.14.0, json_annotation→4.12.0, flutter_svg→2.3.0, cupertino_icons→1.0.9, async→2.13.1, webview_flutter→4.13.1, flutter_native_splash→2.4.8, skeletonizer→2.1.3, postgres→3.5.11, connectivity_plus→7.1.1, file_selector→1.1.0` + the **5 Firebase** minors (`firebase_core→4.9.0`, `firebase_analytics→12.4.1`, `firebase_crashlytics→5.2.2`, `firebase_messaging→16.2.2`, `firebase_performance→0.11.4+1` — bump as a co-versioned set). `build_runner→2.15.0` only after confirming #3142's riverpod_generator bug is gone (test codegen).

### 🟡 Tier 2 — major bumps, plugin-only (read changelog, likely mechanical)
Breaking changes usually in native setup, not Dart API. Each its own PR:
`device_info_plus 10→13` (+3 majors, biggest gap), `file_picker 10→11`, `flutter_secure_storage 9→10`, `package_info_plus 9→10`, `share_plus 12→13`, `flutter_web_auth_2 4→5`.

### 🔴 Tier 3 — major bumps needing real code review
- **`go_router 16→17`** — routing is load-bearing (typed routes, redirects, ShellRoute). v17 has API changes; needs careful migration + full nav testing.
- **`riverpod_generator + riverpod_annotation 3→4`** — codegen contract change; regenerate everything + verify; couple with runtime `flutter_riverpod 3.0.3→3.3.1`. This is also where the build_runner #3142 cap lives — untangle first.
- **`google_fonts 6→8`** (+2 majors) — API/asset-loading changes; verify Pacifico / Inter / BricolageGrotesque still resolve.

### 📝 Worth a look
`hive_ce 2.6→2.19` (+13 minors — large drift on our persistence layer; changelog scan), `drift 2.31→2.33` (paired with drift_dev, regen), `patrol 4.2→4.6` (+4, integration-test harness), `sqlite3_flutter_libs→0.6.0+eol` (the `+eol` tag is a flag — check what's deprecated).

---

## Proposed sequencing

1. **Ship the Flutter 3.44 bump alone first** — clean, low-risk, unblocks nothing else.
2. **Then Tier 1** as one "dependency housekeeping" PR — fast, high-confidence.
3. **Then Tier 2/3 individually**, each with its own changelog read + targeted tests. Never batch a major bump with anything else (one-line `git bisect` when something breaks).

---

## Questions for @hm21

1. **build_runner cap (#3142):** I verified the cap doesn't block Dart 3.12, so I'd keep it as-is for the bump. But do you want to bundle an attempt to *lift* it (test whether riverpod_generator 4.x fixes the `InvalidTypeException`) into the riverpod 3→4 PR, or keep that entirely separate?
2. **go_router 16→17 + riverpod 3→4:** these are the two Tier-3 items that touch app/generated code. Any preference on order, or known landmines in our routing/state layers I should plan around?
3. **media stack:** anything in `media_kit` / `media_kit_video` fork / `pro_video_editor` / `pro_image_editor` you'd want explicitly exercised on 3.44 before we cut over (beyond the standard build + test)?
4. **Sequencing:** does "Flutter bump solo → Tier 1 sweep → Tier 2/3 individually" match how you'd want this staged?

> Note: confidence is ~1.0 on the inventory and static compatibility; "compiles + tests pass" and the Tier 2/3 "upgrades without breaking our code" claims are exactly what the per-PR build/test gates establish — not assertable statically.

issue.title: test(services): cover VideoCircuitBreaker state machine + mixin (#4337)
issue.body:
## Description

Adds unit coverage for `mobile/lib/services/circuit_breaker_service.dart`
(`VideoCircuitBreaker` + `CircuitBreakerMixin`), which was **untested** despite
gating whether failing video URLs get retried.

**25 cases:**

- **Synchronous logic** (real time): initial closed state, failure counting +
  `maxFailureHistory` cap, opening after the recent-failure threshold,
  permanent-failure after `threshold*2`, the per-url exponential-backoff block
  while half-open, `recordSuccess` counter reset, `failureRate` scaling + clamp
  at 100, `getStats`/`getDetailedStats`, `reset`, and `clearPermanentFailures`.
- **Timer-driven transitions** via `fakeAsync` (per #4337 WS-2 async policy —
  `fakeAsync` for timer-driven code, not wall-clock waits): `open→halfOpen`
  after the open timeout, `halfOpen→open` on timeout with no success,
  `halfOpen→closed` after the required successes, and `dispose`/`reset`
  cancelling the recovery timer.
- **`CircuitBreakerMixin`**: fail-open before init, delegation after init,
  success-reset, and teardown.

No production code change — tests only. Uses no mocks (the breaker has no
injected collaborators beyond the logger).

**Related Issue:** Relates to #4337 / #4838 (WS-3 untested-services paydown).
Drops `circuit_breaker_service` from `untested_services.txt` after ratchet PR
#4835 merges.

## Out of Scope

- The remaining untested services (#4838).
- The unreachable "backoff window expired → allow" sub-branch, which depends on
  real `DateTime.now()` the service reads directly (no injected clock); covered
  the reachable "within backoff → block" path instead.

## Verification

- `flutter test test/services/circuit_breaker_service_test.dart` → **25/25 pass**.
- `flutter analyze` clean.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✅ Tests (no production code change)

## Description

Adds unit coverage for `mobile/lib/services/effective_content_labels.dart`,
which was **untested** despite gating NSFW/sensitive-content visibility — it
builds the effective moderation label set for a `VideoEvent` by merging creator
self-labels, trusted kind-1985 labels (by addressable id / event id / content
hash / pubkey), and the `#nsfw`/`#adult` hashtag fallback.

**24 cases** across both public functions:

- **`normalizeModerationLabelValue`** — null/empty/whitespace → null; canonical

  `gore`→`graphic-media`, `pornography`/`explicit`→`porn`, `hate-speech`→`hate`,

- **`resolveEffectiveContentLabels`** — creator self-labels; the four
  moderation-service lookups; `#nsfw`/`#adult` hashtag fallback; source priority
  ordering; de-duplication across sources; and the skip paths when
  `addressableId`/`sha256` are absent or empty.

Uses a hand-written fake for `ModerationLabelService` (the function consumes only
its 4 lookup getters; `noSuchMethod` covers the rest), so no codegen and no real

issue.title: ci(test): test-debt ratchet batch — freeze skips, Future.delayed & untested services (#4337)
issue.body:
## Description

First execution slice of epic **#4337** (testing-debt decomposition): three
**shrink-only LIST ratchets** that freeze the current test-debt at its baseline
so it can only ever go down, wired into the existing `generated-files` CI job.

Epic #4337's 8 leaf issues were administratively closed-as-superseded ~4 min
after the epic opened, without the work being done. 92% of the ~166 skipped
tests carry an identical machine-generated `// TODO(any): Fix and re-enable`
with no owner — the residue of a bulk skip-the-reds sweep. `check_todos.sh`
globs `lib/` only and isn't CI-wired, so `test/` debt accrued unguarded. **This
PR stops the bleeding before paydown begins** (paydown is tracked as child
issues under #4337).

### The three ratchets (clone the proven `check_ui_service_boundary.sh` LIST form)

| Ratchet | Freezes | Baseline | Detector |
|---|---|---|---|
| **WS-1** skip-ceiling | 87 test files with a test-level `skip:` | `baseline/skip_tests.txt` | `grep [(, ]skip: (true\|'\|")` over `*_test.dart` |
| **WS-2** Future.delayed-ceiling | 40 test files (incl. helpers/mocks) using `Future.delayed` | `baseline/future_delayed_tests.txt` | `grep Future\.delayed` over test `*.dart` |
| **WS-3** untested-services-floor | 61 `lib/services` with no same-named test | `baseline/untested_services.txt` | basename set-difference (`comm -23`) |

Shared `scripts/lib/list_ratchet.sh` engine implements NEW / STALE / GROWTH:
- **NEW** — a current offender not in the in-branch baseline → fail.
- **STALE** — a baselined entry that's been fixed/removed → fail (shrink the baseline to lock the win).
- **GROWTH** — the in-branch baseline grew vs `origin/main` → fail (closes the regenerate-and-commit bypass).
- **Fails closed** if `origin/main`'s baseline can't be loaded (CI never silently skips the ratchet); bootstrap-skips the growth check on this introducing commit.

The detectors deliberately exclude non-debt: platform-conditional skips
(`skip: !kIsWeb`), argument-noise (`skipOffstage:`), the `Future.delayed`
detector's own fixtures, `*.md`/`*.archived`/`*.disabled`, and generated files.
`untested_services.txt` annotates the ~10 permanent entries (`# noise:` stubs/
models/mixins/web-shims) and the reshaping-bound ones (`# defer: #4338`/`#4339`,
`# decision: OD-2` for `social_service`).

**Related Issue:** Relates to #4337 (WS-1/WS-2/WS-3). Paydown + remaining
workstreams (WS-4 coverage floors, WS-5 golden, WS-6 integration, WS-7 test-org)
tracked as child issues.

## Out of Scope

- **Paying down** the frozen debt (un-skipping, migrating to fakeAsync/
  pumpEventQueue, writing service tests) — separate child issues; this PR only
  freezes + guards.
- App-level (`mobile/lib`) coverage gate, golden re-enable, integration lane —
  later workstreams.
- The existing `vgv-tag-gate` integer ratchet (unchanged; not co-edited).

## Verification

- All three ratchets pass locally against their fresh baselines (bootstrap note,
  no NEW/STALE).
- NEW and STALE detection exercised by injection (add a `skip:`/`Future.delayed`
  → fails; restore → passes).
- Refactor to the shared engine is **behavior-preserving**: `skip_tests.txt`
  regenerates byte-identical; `UPDATE_BASELINE` is idempotent (fixed a latent
  reason-whitespace growth bug).
- `bash -n` clean on all 4 scripts; `actionlint` clean on the workflow (no new
  findings beyond the pre-existing custom-runner-label notes).
- No Dart changed — pure shell + YAML + baseline data.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✅ Build configuration change
- [x] 🧹 Code refactor (extract shared ratchet engine)

issue.title: epic(testing): reduce skipped coverage debt and stabilize test infrastructure
issue.body:
## Summary

Testing debt is currently spread across skipped tests, missing service coverage, flaky timing patterns, weak integration coverage, and CI enforcement gaps. This needs one parent issue so testing work can be sequenced intentionally instead of living as scattered audit fragments.

This issue is the source of truth for testing and CI debt reduction.

## Problem

Current problems include:
- too many skipped tests with no active execution path
- large service areas with weak or missing direct coverage
- test timing patterns that create flakiness or overhead
- insufficient integration coverage for important runtime flows
- CI coverage policy that is still inconsistent across scopes

## Scope

- reduce skipped test debt
- improve direct coverage for untested services and flows
- replace timing-based test patterns where appropriate
- restore or retire stale test suites intentionally
- tighten CI coverage expectations where it improves signal

## Existing Related Work

- `#3608`
- `#3609`
- `#3610`
- `#3612`
- `#3614`
- `#3616`
- `#3576`
- `#3577`

## Acceptance Criteria

- major testing debt categories are coordinated under one parent issue
- skipped/untested/flaky/CI coverage work has a clear execution home
- related audit leaves can be closed or superseded into this epic
- future test cleanup work has an obvious place to land

## Done When

- testing debt is organized into a manageable execution model
- the repo has fewer ambiguous “someday test cleanup” issues
- the highest-value testing improvements are decomposed into concrete child work

---

## Assignee
`@NotThatKindOfDrLiz`

## Weekly Priority
`P2`

## Weekly Priority Meaning
- `P1` means top priority for the week.
- `P2` means complete this week after P1 priorities are finished.

## Execution Order
1. define triage policy for skipped and stale tests
2. group and supersede scattered testing audit leaves
3. execute the highest-signal coverage and infrastructure fixes first

## Subgroup
- `@NotThatKindOfDrLiz` — DRI
- `@realmeylisdev` — CI/test execution support
- `@untreu2` — coverage and test cleanup support

## Coordination
The listed subgroup must review scope, sequencing, and ownership before implementation starts. Coordination may be synchronous or asynchronous. Do not wait for central coordination if the subgroup can resolve the question directly. Escalate only when blocked or when a testing policy decision is genuinely needed.

## Agent Execution Notes
Agents working from this issue must:
- treat this issue as the coordination source of truth for testing debt cleanup
- prefer meaningful signal over raw test count growth
- delete or retire dead/low-value tests when that is the right outcome
- avoid preserving stale test debt just because it already exists

## Engineering Standard
This work must not create new technical debt.

Where relevant, use the audit issues created from PR `#3530` by `@omartinma` as the source of truth for debt repayment and refactor expectations in this area.

ratchet step or a coverage gate) — no integer-only or "superseded"-only closures.

### Owner-decisions needed (cannot be settled by investigation)
- **OD-1** (DRI + @realmeylisdev): integration runner tier — hosted-swiftshader vs
  GPU self-hosted vs local-only. Gates WS-6's device lane.
- **OD-2** (code owner): `social_service` (3 callers, no live consumer) keep-vs-delete
  before WS-3 tests it.
- **OD-3** (DRI / #4338): the 5 no-test production packages — test vs retire.
- **OD-6** (DRI): confirm #3576/#3577 were falsely closed (not de-scoped).

App-level `mobile/lib` coverage gate (currently 0%) is a separate follow-up.

issue.title: ci(#4337 WS-7): guard test/ structure (test/unit re-accretion)
issue.body:
Parent epic: #4337.

A big-bang test-tree reshuffle is **won't-do** (huge low-value diffs that collide
with every in-flight test PR). Instead, guard against regression and clean up
opportunistically.

### Tasks
1. Ratchet that guards against **re-creating `test/unit/`** (45 files — the real
   non-mirroring accretion vector, not just root-loose files). Clone the LIST engine.
2. Enforce mirror-structure (`test/` mirrors `lib/`) in the WS-3 review checklist.
3. Opportunistic, low-risk moves: the 6 loose files with obvious `lib/` homes;
   read each colliding same-name pair side-by-side and **delete stale duplicates**
   rather than `group()`-merging.

Supersedes closed leaf #3614 (do not reopen). Effort: S.

issue.title: test(#4337 WS-6): expand integration coverage (headless service/widget lane)
issue.body:
Parent epic: #4337.

Today integration has **~0 CI execution**: `mobile_ci` excludes `integration`;
the service workflow is `workflow_dispatch`-only and runs the **1** `--tags service`
file. 29 Patrol device tests run only locally (`-gpu host`).

### Proceed now (no owner-gate)
- Expand the headless `--tags service` lane + widget-level integration tests.
- Per-file tag split (do not blanket-tag): `deleted_video…`→`service`;
  `video_creation_flow`→rewrite/delete (stub); `c2pa_init`→`device`/`hardware` (StrongBox, #2019).
- Highest-value flows: feed TTFF, record→publish, auth journey.

### Owner-gate (OD-1, DRI + @realmeylisdev) — blocks the device lane
Stand up an Android-emulator lane at all, and if so: (A) hosted Linux + KVM +
`-gpu swiftshader_indirect` (cheap; ExoPlayer/camera at risk) vs (B) GPU
self-hosted (reliable incl. the 41 camera cases; real \$\$) vs (C) stay local-only
+ invest in service/widget lanes. CI-minute/spend/flake ROI call.

issue.title: test(#4337 WS-5): re-enable the golden test suite (l10n wrapper fix + regen + tag gate)
issue.body:
Parent epic: #4337.

Root cause is **stale-by-neglect**, not a render-delta: the golden wrapper lacks
`AppLocalizations.localizationsDelegates`/`supportedLocales` → null-check throw +
`RenderFlex` overflow. The l10n-aware wrapper already exists in
`golden_test_helpers.dart`'s `matchesGolden` extension.

### Tasks (16 skipped `testGoldens` cases)
1. Lift the l10n-aware wrapper into the shared `materialAppWrapper` path; fix overflow.
2. `flutter test --update-goldens` on CI-pinned Flutter **3.41.9**; commit masters.
3. Remove `skip:`; add `tags: TestTag.golden` to every case.
4. Add a **golden-tag gate** (untagged golden call sites must stay 0).
5. DELETE the 32 `test/goldens/widgets/failures/` debug artifacts + orphaned masters.

### Residual spike (B5)
After regen on Linux CI, check for a true macOS-vs-Linux font/AA delta — fallback
is a committed `flutter_test_config.dart` tolerance. Effort: M.

issue.title: ci(#4337 WS-4): coverage-floor ratchet + raise measured package floors
issue.body:
Parent epic: #4337.

Per-package coverage is enforced via `very_good test --coverage --min-coverage <N>`
(default 100 when omitted); the **mobile/ app itself enforces NO floor**
(`mobile_ci.yaml` tests job has no `--coverage`).

### Tasks
1. **Ratchet:** `mobile/scripts/baseline/coverage_floors.txt` (`packages/<pkg> <floor>`,
   omitted⇒100) + `check_coverage_floors.sh` (clone the LIST engine); **forbid-lowering**
   a floor (a drop must lower the baseline in-diff with justification).
2. **Raise now (CI-exact measured, config-only):** `models` 25→60, `permissions_service`
   22→36, `unified_logger` 40→42 (pair with tests — only ~3pt slack).
3. **Measure-in-PR then pin to measured−1pp:** `video_event_cache` (floor 0),
   `nostr_sdk` (20), `db_client` (40), `keycast_flutter`/`funnelcake_api_client` (44).

### Owner-decisions
- **OD-3:** the 5 no-test production packages (`content_blocklist_service`,
  `curation_service`, `nostr_apps`, `nostr_gateway`, `sticker_pack_repository`) —
  test vs retire vs #4338.
- App-level (`mobile/lib`) coverage gate is a **separate follow-up** (suite already

issue.title: test(#4337 WS-3): test the ~50 untested services + resolve social_service (OD-2)
issue.body:
Parent epic: #4337 · Freeze/guard shipped in PR #4835.

The untested-services-floor ratchet froze 61 `lib/services` entries with no
same-named test in `mobile/scripts/baseline/untested_services.txt` (~10 are
`# noise:` permanent; several `# defer: #4338`/`#4339`). Write tests for the
~50 genuinely-testable, stable services — each shrinks the floor.

### Gates / priorities
- **OD-2 (owner-decision):** `social_service` has 3 callers and no live consumer —
  decide keep-vs-delete **before** writing its test. Delete if dead (no throwaway
  tests).
- Prioritize `effective_content_labels` (live NSFW-gating, untested) and the
  auth/nostr-publishing/cache clusters.

issue.title: test(#4337 WS-2): migrate the 40 frozen Future.delayed test files to fakeAsync/pumpEventQueue
issue.body:
Parent epic: #4337 · Freeze/guard shipped in PR #4835.

The Future.delayed-ceiling ratchet froze 40 test files (tests + hand-written
helpers/mocks) in `mobile/scripts/baseline/future_delayed_tests.txt`. Migrate
them off wall-clock waits — each migration shrinks the baseline.

### Async policy (pinned)
- **`pumpEventQueue`** for stream-settling (the dominant pattern — real
  `StreamController` async generators).
- **`fakeAsync`** for timer/timeout-driven cases.
- Blanket `fakeAsync` is the wrong tool for stream cases; reviewers will reject it.

### Detector tool fate
Decide `mobile/test/tools/future_delayed_detector_test.dart` (currently skipped):
keep for `--suggest/--fix` migration affordances, or delete + rely on the LIST
ratchet. Do not leave it `skip: true` + `TODO(any)`.

### DoD
Each slice shrinks `baseline/future_delayed_tests.txt` (CI enforces). Done when
the baseline holds only legitimate real-IO waits (if any), all documented.

issue.title: test(#4337 WS-1): triage and pay down the 87 frozen skipped tests
issue.body:
Parent epic: #4337 · Freeze/guard shipped in PR #4835.

The skip-ceiling ratchet (PR #4835) froze 87 test files carrying a test-level
`skip:` in `mobile/scripts/baseline/skip_tests.txt`. This issue pays the debt
down — every removal shrinks the baseline.

### Approach — apply the decision tree (tasks/plan_4337.md §7), first match wins
1. Empty body / no assertion / tests a removed-or-deprecated feature → **DELETE**
2. Tests a route/screen/widget that no longer exists → **DELETE**
3. Stale duplicate of another test → **DELETE** one
4. Real platform/network/hardware dependency → **QUARANTINE** behind a tag, not `skip:`
5. Broken-after-refactor, behavior still wanted → **REWRITE**
6. Genuinely flaky timing → fix with `pumpEventQueue`/`fakeAsync`, then **RECOVER**

Start with an empirical un-skip-and-classify pass over the router/screen/widget
cluster (~55-70 files) — an unknown share are case-2 DELETEs. 92% currently carry
a no-owner `// TODO(any): Fix and re-enable`.

### Detector / DoD
`grep -rnE "[(, ]skip: (true|'|\")" mobile/test` ; ship in slices, each shrinking
`baseline/skip_tests.txt` (CI enforces no NEW/STALE/GROWTH). Done when the
baseline is empty or only intentional quarantines (tagged) remain.

issue.title: style(design-system): migrate raw Icons.* to DivineIcon across settings
issue.body:
Part of #4803

## Summary

Sweeps 31 raw Material `Icons.*` uses to `DivineIcon` across the seven settings screens / dialogs touched by the in-flight Cubit migration PRs (#4791, #4792, #4793, #4794, #4795, #4798). Closes the design-system gap surfaced by the audit on those branches.

Files touched:
- `lib/screens/safety_settings_screen.dart`
- `lib/screens/blossom_settings_screen.dart`
- `lib/screens/settings/content_preferences_screen.dart`
- `lib/screens/sounds_screen.dart`
- `lib/screens/relay_settings_screen.dart`
- `lib/widgets/save_original_progress_sheet.dart`
- `lib/widgets/watermark_download_progress_sheet.dart`

## Migration table

| Material `Icons.*` | `DivineIconName` |
| --- | --- |
| add | plus |
| arrow_forward | arrowRight |
| check_circle | checkCircle |
| chevron_right | caretRight |
| delete | trash |
| error_outline | warningCircle |
| expand_more | caretDown |
| filter_list | funnelSimple |
| info_outline | info |
| language | globe |
| lock_outline | lockSimple |
| music_note | musicNote |
| refresh | arrowClockwise |
| restore | arrowCounterClockwise |
| search | search |
| share | share |
| verified | sealCheck |
| verified_user | shieldCheck |

## Out of scope (follow-up)

Two pieces of design-system debt that surfaced in the audit but aren't fixed here:

1. **Icons without a `divine_ui` equivalent.** Left as `Icons.*`: `add_circle_outline`, `cloud_done`, `cloud_off`, `cloud_upload`, `label_outline`, `local_fire_department`, `mic`, `music_off`, `open_in_new`, `people`, `radio_button_checked`, `radio_button_off`, `remove_circle_outline`, `search_off`, `star`. Needs new SVG assets added to `divine_ui` — designer work. **Tracked in #4833** (sub-issue of #4803).
2. **Inline `TextStyle(...)` → `VineTheme.*Font()` migration.** 115 sites across these 10 files; deferred because the helpers bake in explicit fontFamily/size/weight/lineHeight/letterSpacing and many existing color-only `TextStyle(color: X)` rely on Material's inherited defaults. Migrating blindly risks visual regression across 10 screens. Wants a designer pass / golden tests first.

## Coordination with the in-flight Cubit PRs

This PR touches the same lines that the 7 open Cubit-migration PRs (#4791, #4792, #4793, #4794, #4795, #4798) verbatim-relocate from `_build*` helper methods to private widget classes. **Either ordering is fine but produces conflicts:**

- If this lands first → each Cubit PR needs a trivial rebase that picks `DivineIcon(icon: …)` over the old `Icon(Icons.*)` at the new widget-class locations.
- If a Cubit PR lands first → this PR rebases and re-applies the same mappings to the new widget-class locations.

The migrated icons are pure visual swaps — no behavior change — so resolution is mechanical.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze` on all touched files: clean
- [x] `flutter test test/screens/safety_settings_screen_test.dart` — 10 pass
- [x] `flutter test test/screens/settings_screen_audio_sharing_test.dart` — 5 pass
- [x] `flutter test test/screens/sounds_screen_test.dart` — 27 pass
- [x] `flutter test test/screens/relay_settings_screen_layout_test.dart` — 22 pass
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/save_original_progress_sheet_test.dart` — pass
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/watermark_download_progress_sheet_test.dart` — pass
- [ ] Visual smoke: run the app and walk through each screen to confirm icon glyphs render at the expected size/color

issue.title: Add 15 missing settings icons to divine_ui (unblocks Icons.* sweep)

labels.name: divine_ui
labels.description: Flutter UI component library for Divine

issue.body:
**Parent**: #4803 (Migrate raw `Icons.*` to `DivineIcon` across the codebase)

## Problem

The settings-screens slice of the `Icons.* → DivineIcon` sweep (PR #4802) left **15 Material icons untouched** because `divine_ui`'s `DivineIconName` enum has no equivalent SVG asset. These callsites stay as raw `Icons.*` and can't pick up design-system stroke/style updates, creating the same drift #4803 / #3649 / #3652 track. They can only be migrated once the assets exist in `divine_ui`, so they're split out here as the designer-scoped prerequisite.

## Missing icons

Verified against the `DivineIconName` enum in `mobile/packages/divine_ui/lib/src/icon/divine_icon.dart` — none have a clean 1:1 match today:

| Material `Icons.*` | Used in (settings slice) |
| --- | --- |
| `add_circle_outline` | `safety_settings_screen.dart` |
| `remove_circle_outline` | `safety_settings_screen.dart` |
| `label_outline` | `safety_settings_screen.dart` |
| `people` | `safety_settings_screen.dart` |
| `cloud_upload` | `blossom_settings_screen.dart` |
| `cloud_done` | `relay_settings_screen.dart` |
| `cloud_off` | `relay_settings_screen.dart` |
| `open_in_new` | `relay_settings_screen.dart` |
| `mic` | `content_preferences_screen.dart` |
| `radio_button_checked` | `content_preferences_screen.dart` |
| `radio_button_off` | `content_preferences_screen.dart` |
| `local_fire_department` | `sounds_screen.dart` |
| `music_off` | `sounds_screen.dart` |
| `search_off` | `sounds_screen.dart` |
| `star` | `sounds_screen.dart` |

These 15 also appear across other (not-yet-swept) screens — the asset additions unblock the whole-codebase sweep tracked by #4803, not just the settings slice.

## Near-equivalents to confirm before commissioning new SVGs

A few have a *near* match already in the enum — design should decide whether the existing glyph is acceptable rather than adding a redundant asset:

- `open_in_new` → `arrowUpRight` / `linkSimple` / `shareNetwork`
- `star` → `sparkle` (different glyph; likely needs a true star)
- `radio_button_checked` / `radio_button_off` → `selection` / `selectionFill` (different semantics)
- `add_circle_outline` / `remove_circle_outline` → there's `plus` / `minus` but no circled variant

## Definition of done

1. Designer provides SVGs for the confirmed-missing icons (Phosphor-style, matching the existing `divine_ui` icon set).
2. Assets added to `divine_ui` and wired into the `DivineIconName` enum + `assetPath` switch, with matching tests (`divine_ui` is a **strict-100%-coverage** package).
3. Follow-up sweep PR replaces the 15 `Icons.*` callsites with `DivineIcon(...)` and ticks them off under #4803.

## Source

Surfaced by the PR #4802 review (rabble-claw, 2026-05-30): leftover no-equivalent icons should be tracked explicitly, not left as "known debt in a PR description."

**Parent**: #4803 (Migrate raw `Icons.*` to `DivineIcon` across the codebase)

## Problem

The settings-screens slice of the `Icons.* → DivineIcon` sweep (PR #4802) left **15 Material icons untouched** because `divine_ui`'s `DivineIconName` enum has no equivalent SVG asset. These callsites stay as raw `Icons.*` and can't pick up design-system stroke/style updates, creating the same drift #4803 / #3649 / #3652 track. They can only be migrated once the assets exist in `divine_ui`, so they're split out here as the designer-scoped prerequisite.

## Missing icons

Verified against the `DivineIconName` enum in `mobile/packages/divine_ui/lib/src/icon/divine_icon.dart` — none have a clean 1:1 match today:

| Material `Icons.*` | Used in (settings slice) |
| --- | --- |
| `add_circle_outline` | `safety_settings_screen.dart` |
| `remove_circle_outline` | `safety_settings_screen.dart` |
| `label_outline` | `safety_settings_screen.dart` |
| `people` | `safety_settings_screen.dart` |
| `cloud_upload` | `blossom_settings_screen.dart` |
| `cloud_done` | `relay_settings_screen.dart` |
| `cloud_off` | `relay_settings_screen.dart` |
| `open_in_new` | `relay_settings_screen.dart` |
| `mic` | `content_preferences_screen.dart` |
| `radio_button_checked` | `content_preferences_screen.dart` |
| `radio_button_off` | `content_preferences_screen.dart` |
| `local_fire_department` | `sounds_screen.dart` |
| `music_off` | `sounds_screen.dart` |
| `search_off` | `sounds_screen.dart` |
| `star` | `sounds_screen.dart` |

These 15 also appear across other (not-yet-swept) screens — the asset additions unblock the whole-codebase sweep tracked by #4803, not just the settings slice.

## Near-equivalents to confirm before commissioning new SVGs

A few have a *near* match already in the enum — design should decide whether the existing glyph is acceptable rather than adding a redundant asset:

- `open_in_new` → `arrowUpRight` / `linkSimple` / `shareNetwork`
- `star` → `sparkle` (different glyph; likely needs a true star)
- `radio_button_checked` / `radio_button_off` → `selection` / `selectionFill` (different semantics)
- `add_circle_outline` / `remove_circle_outline` → there's `plus` / `minus` but no circled variant

## Definition of done

1. Designer provides SVGs for the confirmed-missing icons (Phosphor-style, matching the existing `divine_ui` icon set).
2. Assets added to `divine_ui` and wired into the `DivineIconName` enum + `assetPath` switch, with matching tests (`divine_ui` is a **strict-100%-coverage** package).
3. Follow-up sweep PR replaces the 15 `Icons.*` callsites with `DivineIcon(...)` and ticks them off under #4803.

## Source

Surfaced by the PR #4802 review (rabble-claw, 2026-05-30): leftover no-equivalent icons should be tracked explicitly, not left as "known debt in a PR description."
